title: The buddy system
coreMove: Invite a trusted challenger to audit the story before ego edits it clean.
sourcePressure: The chapter shows why solo review bends around ego and why a trusted challenger can test assumptions, confidence, and after-the-fact rewrites.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must make challenge feel allied with accuracy; a buddy is not merely the person who makes the protagonist feel better.

sourceAnchors.name: the buddy system
sourceAnchors.detail: The source defines the buddy system as an outside correction tool for forecasts, evidence, confidence, and post-outcome revision.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The right buddy is a hand on the file before your ego starts cleaning the pages.

sourceAnchors.name: outside challenge of self-serving narration
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says solo reflection bends too easily around ego, so another person must test the story.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A private explanation can sound clean because no one else has asked where the dirt went.

sourceAnchors.name: truth-seeking correction
sourceAnchors.detail: The source separates correction from reassurance: real help challenges the comfortable version in service of accuracy.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Comfort may settle the nerves; correction makes the estimate answer for itself.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: documentary edit room deciding whether a scene is fair
exampleSpecs.audience: creative teams handling real people’s stories
exampleSpecs.stakes: a dramatic scene could mislead viewers and damage a subject’s reputation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel pauses the timeline and asks her editor to name what footage would weaken her preferred cut before she exports it.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The edit suite is dark except for a paused frame on a woman’s face.

exampleSpecs.domain: freelance tax estimate before quarterly filing
exampleSpecs.stakes: a comforting estimate could become a penalty notice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You ask Mikkel to show the invoice stack to the colleague who questions his deductions, not the friend who says it is probably fine.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You have a shoebox of receipts and one number that feels too painless.

exampleSpecs.domain: surgical resident preparing for a difficult procedure simulation
exampleSpecs.stakes: confidence from easy praise could hide a weak handoff before a high-risk simulation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Laura chooses the attending who will stop the rehearsal at the first vague instruction and make her repeat the handoff until the risk is named.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The simulation lab smells faintly of disinfectant and warm plastic.

exampleSpecs.domain: patent pitch practice before investor due diligence
exampleSpecs.stakes: an untested novelty claim could collapse in due diligence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 11:13 a.m., Henrik invites the engineer who doubts the novelty claim to interrogate slide seven before the investor does.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 11:13 a.m., Henrik leaves slide seven on the projector and closes his laptop halfway.

exampleSpecs.domain: mountain rescue route plan before a winter training exercise
exampleSpecs.stakes: a team may mistake morale for route safety in worsening weather
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya changes the route review after her partner asks which slope condition would make her abandon the plan before anyone leaves the trailhead.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Aanya one whiteout drill to stop treating morale as evidence.

exampleSpecs.domain: community choir audition selection after a favorite singer stumbles
exampleSpecs.stakes: personal affection could distort a fair casting decision
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What would David’s choice look like if his assistant compared the score sheet with the private note he wrote before the audition?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What does a score sheet know that affection wants to blur?

skillTargets: use buddy questions before and after outcomes

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next consequential call, write the one assumption carrying the most weight and send only that assumption to a trusted challenger with the question: what would make this false?
